# tests/fixtures/lists — mini word-list fixture for the seed builder

A scaled-down `data/lists/` with the same shapes (PLAN §4.1; `design/word-lists/SYNTHESIS.md` §3.2): a `format: 2`
manifest, six lists, `aliases.tsv`, `overrides.tsv`, `SHA256SUMS`, plus a previous seed and a mini ECDICT so that
`backend/tests/unit/test_seedbuild_build.py` (slice S3b) can run `wd.seedbuild.build` end to end without the 851 MB
`stardict.db`. Generated by the S3a slice from the delivered files; every list line is a **verbatim** line of the
corresponding `data/lists` file, every previous-seed record a verbatim record of `data/seed/vocab.jsonl.gz` (v1 keys),
every ECDICT row a verbatim row of ECDICT 1.0.28 (`test_seedbuild_normalise.py` pins all three; the one `\r\n` inside ECDICT's `a`
translation is spelled `char(13, 10)` in the SQL, so the value survives a text-mode read and the file stays LF-only).

## Expected membership (rules + mini ECDICT + previous seed; the build adds CET flags from `previous_seed.jsonl`)

Computed with `wd.seedbuild.normalise` (`split_head` / `resolve_phrase` / `inherit_forms`) over this directory. 82 members,
32 of them new rows (`NEW`); `bookshelf`, `hotdog`, `humourous` are retained without a stage (`stages` from CET flags only).

Build-time log expected from this directory: appendix `skipped` = `pla day`, `mount huangshan`; R12 `rejected` = `The United
States of America` (head, 5 tokens), `United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization` (variant, charset),
`add ... to` (phrase, punctuation token); `unparsed_notes` = `Before the Common Era`; phrases skipped = `a lot of/lots of`
(other), `add...to` and `agree with sb.` (patterns); aliases written = `mr`→`mr.`, `pe`→`p.e.`, `hot-dog`→`hot dog`,
`humourous`→`humorous` (the last one is itself a previous lemma, so the importer's headword guard skips its `word_forms`
row).

To regenerate after changing the picks, edit the key lists in the S3a generator (kept in the session scratchpad as
`s3a/gen_fixtures.py`; its `q()` spells a CR inside a value as `char(13, 10)`) or re-pick verbatim lines by hand and refresh
`SHA256SUMS` with `shasum -a 256`.
